layout_thesis.statement: The academy sells two things that look different but are one promise: bring a player to Spain, or take a Spanish coach to a club. The site is built as a pair of routes from one centre. It sits on the brand's primary colourway — gold on dark forest green — because that is what the identity board leads with and because it is what makes the brand's own accent usable: gold measures 4.94:1 on the dark ground against 2.22:1 on the cream one. Hierarchy comes from one ink at many strengths rather than from a palette, which on dark reaches further down the ladder. Photography is client-supplied and phone-grade, so it appears only small and inset — never full-bleed, never above the fold — and the pages carry themselves on type and structure instead.
layout_thesis.audience: Two readers with one question each. An international player asking whether a training week in Spain will actually be built around them, and a club director asking whether flying in a coach for nine days will leave their own coaching better than it found it.
layout_thesis.job_to_be_done: Make a stranger believe that a programme will be shaped around them specifically, then get them to write an email.
layout_thesis.why_this_not_generic: A generic academy site opens on a full-bleed action photograph, states three adjectives, and lists facilities. This one cannot use that photograph — the available images are phone snapshots and the sharpest carries another brand's sponsor livery — so it leads with the one thing that is genuinely specific: twelve years, one town, and programmes quoted per client rather than sold as packages. The two services get separate pages because they address different buyers, and the shared credibility (Marbella, NAC, M3) sits on a third.

signature_element.name: The ball monogram
signature_element.description: A stroked circle crossed by two opposed seams — a padel ball reduced to three lines — drawn in gold and used once per page as the optical counterweight to the headline.
signature_element.why_it_fits_brand: It is the client's own identity, taken from the designer's brand board where the rationale is written as 'Inspiración en la pelota' and 'minimalismo y elegancia'. It is the only mark the brand actually owns, and it survives being drawn at any size because it is three strokes.
signature_element.implementation_note: Inline SVG in --color-primary, sized with clamp() so it scales with the headline. Not the supplied JPEG: that file is a flattened screenshot of a presentation board, and a raster of a slide is not a logo asset. The original vector should be requested before production.

effects: fade and rise on section entry, under 200ms
one horizontally-scrolling rail per long page, pinned only while it advances
a single marquee band per page as a rule between movements
motion_vocabulary.rationale: The brand voice is a coach's — specific and unhurried. Motion that draws attention to itself would contradict it. Everything here is either an entry fade or a direct response to scrolling; nothing loops in the reader's peripheral vision except the marquee, which is a deliberate separator and stops entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

skipped_sections.reason: The site is a static export with no server, so a form needs an external endpoint bound to an account the client has not supplied. Inventing a Formspree or Basin ID would produce a form that silently discards every submission, which is worse than no form. A WhatsApp link is impossible for the same reason in a different direction: no phone number appears anywhere in the source material. The published email address is rendered as a mailto: link instead.
No customer quotes exist anywhere in the client's material and the brief explicitly forbids inventing any. Method and named affiliations are used as the honest substitute for social proof.

The brief asks for a professional image gallery, but the ten supplied images are WhatsApp-compressed phone snapshots at 1536px or less, several are stills lifted from video, and the sharpest landscape is dominated by third-party sponsor branding that does not belong to this brand. A gallery presents images as the subject, which these cannot survive. They are better used small and incidental, or replaced by a commissioned shoot.

The brief describes elite coaches as a service, but no individual coach is named, credentialed or photographed in the supplied material, and it is not established which person in the photographs is the principal. Profiles would require inventing people.

The brief asks for an interactive map, but no street address was supplied — only the town — and an embedded map would add a third-party script and a cookie banner obligation to a static site for no navigational benefit at town resolution.

Privacy policy, cookie policy and legal notice cannot be written without the operating entity's registration details, its data processors and its cookie inventory. A Spanish and EU-facing site needs all three before launch; they are a client input, not a design decision.
No social handles appear anywhere in the client's material. The previous site linked six platforms, every one of them to '#'.

decisions.decision: Open every page on type, with no photography above the fold.
alternatives_considered: Full-bleed hero using the tennis-court sunburst image
Full-bleed hero using the padel facility image with a heavy overlay
Wait for a commissioned photo shoot before building
decisions.why_chosen: A hero image is the least forgiving placement on a site — full width, above the fold, held on screen for the entire first impression. The available images are phone-grade at 1536px or less; the sharpest is covered in OYSHO and Range Rover livery, which would credit those brands rather than this one. Type at display scale cannot fail on resolution, crop or colour cast, and the client's own brand board asks for minimalism, so the constraint and the brief point the same way.

decisions.decision: Split the two services onto separate pages rather than sections of one.
alternatives_considered: One long landing page with both services as sections
One page with a toggle between the two audiences
decisions.why_chosen: They address different buyers with different questions — a player asking whether a week will suit them, a club director asking what nine days leaves behind. On a single page each reader has to skip half the content to find theirs.

decisions.decision: Publish the exclusion about accommodation and restaurants on the same surface as the inclusions.
alternatives_considered: Put it in a footnote or terms page
decisions.why_chosen: It is the client's own wording and it is the sort of thing most academy sites bury until after payment. Stating it beside the inclusions is what makes the inclusions credible, and it costs one sentence.

decisions.decision: Ship a mailto: link instead of a contact form.
alternatives_considered: A Formspree or Basin form with a placeholder endpoint
decisions.why_chosen: A static export cannot receive a POST, and every alternative required inventing something the client has not supplied — an account-bound endpoint ID or a phone number that appears nowhere in the source material. The email address is real and published. The gap is recorded in skipped_sections rather than hidden behind a form that silently drops submissions.

decisions.decision: Use forest green as the ink and gold strictly as a fill, rule and marker.
alternatives_considered: Gold headings on the off-white ground
A dark-mode site with gold text
decisions.why_chosen: Gold on the off-white ground measures 2.25:1, which fails AA and also fails the 3:1 large-text threshold. Using it as text would repeat the invisible-text defect this pipeline has already shipped twice. As a fill it is unrestricted, and text on it uses the derived pairing at 4.94:1.

decisions.decision: Name no individual anywhere on the site.
alternatives_considered: Feature the principal coach as a personal brand
Use the founder portrait on the About page
decisions.why_chosen: At least two different men appear across the supplied photographs and it is not established which, if either, is the principal. Attaching a name to the wrong face is a worse error than an impersonal About page, and the operator chose an academy brand over a personal one.

decisions.decision: Build on the dark forest-green ground rather than the off-white one.
decisions.why_chosen: The brand board's primary colourway is gold on dark green; off-white is secondary. Measured, the dark ground is also the only one on which the brand's accent works as an accent: gold is 2.22:1 on cream (failing AA and the 3:1 large-text threshold) and 4.94:1 on the dark green. The opacity ladder deepens too — the small-text floor moves from /70 to /55 — so hierarchy can come from one ink instead of a second colour. Building light first forced gold out of every text role it was designed for.
